title: Multiplayer HVAC Airflow Particle Visualization
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive multiplayer HVAC airflow particle visualization for a building floor plan. The scene must meet ALL of the following requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Render a top-down orthographic camera view of a simplified rectangular building floor plan (40m x 25m) with 4 rooms separated by interior walls (thin box geometries, gray color #888888).
- Room layout: Room A (top-left, 20x12.5m), Room B (top-right, 20x12.5m), Room C (bottom-left, 20x12.5m), Room D (bottom-right, 20x12.5m).
- Each wall segment is a BoxGeometry with height 3m, thickness 0.3m. Exterior walls are darker gray #555555.
- Each room has one HVAC vent (supply) represented by a small blue box (1m x 1m x 0.2m) placed at the center of the room's ceiling, and one return vent (red box, same size) placed near the room's floor corner.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light from above (intensity 0.8).
- Floor is a plane with light beige color #F5F0E0.

## Particle System
- Each HVAC supply vent emits airflow particles (small spheres, radius 0.08m). Particles are colored by temperature: blue (#0066FF) for cold air (18°C), transitioning through white (#FFFFFF) at 22°C to red (#FF3300) for hot air (28°C). Use linear interpolation for intermediate temperatures.
- Each room maintains a pool of up to 150 particles (600 total max). Particles spawn from supply vents with initial velocity directed downward/outward in a cone pattern (spread angle 45°), speed 0.5-1.5 m/s randomized.
- Particles lose velocity over time (drag coefficient 0.02 per frame), are deflected by walls (elastic reflection), and are absorbed when they reach a return vent (within 1.5m distance).
- Particle lifetime is 8 seconds max; particles fade out (opacity 1.0 to 0.0) over the last 2 seconds.
- Track total kinetic energy of all particles: KE = sum(0.5 * mass * v^2) where mass = 0.01 kg per particle.

## Multiplayer Simulation (Simulated)
- Simulate 2 players: Player 1 (current user, green cursor) and Player 2 (AI-simulated, orange cursor). Each player has a circular cursor (radius 1m) rendered as a flat ring on the floor.
- Player 1 cursor follows the mouse position projected onto the floor plane.
- Player 2 cursor moves autonomously in a slow figure-8 pattern across rooms, completing one loop every 15 seconds.
- Each player can place temporary "fan" objects (yellow arrow helpers, length 2m) that apply a directional force (2.0 N) to nearby particles (within 3m radius). Player 1 places fans with left-click; direction is toward the click point from the cursor center.
- Maximum 4 fans per player (8 total). Fans persist for 12 seconds then auto-remove.
- Player 2 AI places a fan every 5 seconds at its current position, aimed toward the nearest return vent.

## Room Temperature Model
- Each room has a temperature value starting at 24°C. Supply vents cool the room by -0.05°C per active particle per second. Return vents warm the room by +0.02°C per absorbed particle. Fans accelerate mixing (reduce temperature delta toward 22°C target by 0.01°C/s per fan in that room).
- Temperature is clamped to [16°C, 32°C].
- Display each room's temperature as a floating text sprite above the room center.

## User Interactions
- Left-click on floor: Player 1 places a fan at cursor position aimed toward click point.
- Right-click on a fan: removes that fan (undo). Only Player 1's fans can be removed.
- Keyboard 'R': reset all fans for Player 1 (undo all).
- Keyboard '1','2','3','4': toggle individual room HVAC on/off (stops particle emission and fan effects for that room). Default: all ON.
- Keyboard 'T': cycle global temperature preset: Normal(22°C target), Cool(18°C target), Warm(26°C target). This changes supply vent particle temperature.
- Keyboard 'P': pause/resume particle simulation.
- Keyboard 'Space': toggle between top-down orthographic and perspective (45° angle) camera views.
- DOM button 'Reset All': resets entire simulation to initial state.

## HUD / DOM Elements
- Top-left HUD panel (semi-transparent dark background) showing:
  - Total active particles count
  - Total kinetic energy (formatted to 4 decimal places)
  - Current temperature preset name
  - Simulation status (Running/Paused)
- Bottom bar with buttons: 'Reset All', and 4 toggle buttons labeled 'Room A','Room B','Room C','Room D' showing ON/OFF state with green/red backgrounds.
- Player info panel (top-right) showing Player 1 fan count and Player 2 fan count.

## State Management (CRITICAL)
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- particleCount: number (total active particles)
- totalKineticEnergy: number (sum of 0.5*m*v^2 for all particles)
- roomTemperatures: {A: number, B: number, C: number, D: number}
- roomHVACActive: {A: boolean, B: boolean, C: boolean, D: boolean}
- player1FanCount: number
- player2FanCount: number
- temperaturePreset: string ('Normal'|'Cool'|'Warm')
- simulationPaused: boolean
- cameraMode: string ('orthographic'|'perspective')
- player2Position: {x: number, z: number}
- totalFansPlaced: number (cumulative, never decreases)
- totalParticlesAbsorbed: number (cumulative counter)
- frameCount: number (increments each animation frame)
- lastFanPlacedBy: string ('player1'|'player2'|'none')
- particlesPerRoom: {A: number, B: number, C: number, D: number}
- supplyTemperature: number (current supply vent temperature based on preset)
- energyHistory: array of last 10 totalKineticEnergy values
- fanPositions: array of {x, z, dirX, dirZ, owner, roomId} for all active fans
physics_constraints: Particles must obey drag deceleration (v *= (1 - 0.02) per frame). Wall collisions are elastic (velocity component normal to wall is negated). Kinetic energy must be NaN-free and non-negative at all times. Room temperatures must remain in [16, 32] range. Total kinetic energy should generally decrease over time due to drag (energy dissipation) unless fans inject energy. Particle velocities must not exceed 5 m/s (terminal velocity clamp). Conservation check: energy can only increase when fans apply force; otherwise it must monotonically decrease or stay constant within epsilon 0.001.
